name: Pursuit Agent
description: Executes movement commands in real time, continuously, with no turn structure — the counterpart of movement.grid_movement_range for a game that does not take turns. utility.behavior_fsm decides an entity WANTS to close on something and says so on the command bus; that request has to be carried out by somebody, and until this existed the only executor in the catalogue was the turn-based one, which drags combat.action_point_economy and combat.turn_order_queue in behind it. An action game importing a turn queue to make a wolf walk is the wrong answer to the right question. It owns the movement only: whose turn it is is nobody's question here, what the entity wants is the FSM's, where the entity IS belongs to combat.unit_roster, and it emits movement.moveExecuted rather than an event of its own so the roster updates through the same path a tactical move already uses. Reusing that event is the point — a catalogue that invents an event per movement style ends up with two rosters listening to two events about the same fact. It does not decide how far away an entity NOTICES you: utility.behavior_fsm declares detectionRange and publishes it, and this reads it, because a second aggro number living here is a second number to keep in step with the first. Where no FSM is in the build there is nothing to notice with and everything pursues from anywhere, which is the honest fallback and the behaviour every existing build already had. `leashMultiple` is the other half of the same idea and belongs here, because giving up is a movement decision.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: tilesPerSecond
inputs.description: How fast a pursuing entity crosses tiles. A pack that moves faster than the player is a chase nobody wins, so this is the single number that decides whether an encounter is a fight or a funeral.

inputs.name: stopAtRange
inputs.description: Tiles from the target at which pursuit stops. 1 is melee — close enough to strike, not so close the bodies overlap. Anything larger is a ranged attacker that keeps its distance.

inputs.name: repathSeconds
inputs.description: How often a pursuer recomputes its route. Every frame is exact and wasteful; never is a wolf walking confidently into a wall the player stepped behind.

inputs.name: separation
inputs.description: Whether pursuers refuse to stand on each other. Without it a pack converges to one tile and reads as one enemy with several health bars.

inputs.name: leashMultiple
inputs.description: How much further than detectionRange a pursuer will follow before losing interest, as a multiple of it. It exists because one threshold flickers: a target hovering exactly at the edge is noticed, dropped, noticed and dropped, and the enemy reads as broken rather than as cautious. Anything at or below 1 disables the hysteresis and restores that flicker.

outputs.name: pursuing
outputs.description: Entity ids currently closing on something, with their target and distance.

provenance: The gap found building Action RPG: behavior_fsm requested moves, the command bus dispatched them, and nothing in a real-time build executed them.
